title: Language Pack Manifest
description: Top-level descriptor for a language learning pack

schemaVersion.description: Pack format version this manifest conforms to

version.description: Semantic version of this pack release

code.description: ISO 639 code, optional region (e.g. ja, en-US, pt-BR)

name.description: English name of the language (e.g. Japanese)

nativeName.description: Name in the language itself (e.g. 日本語)

script.description: ISO 15924 script code (e.g. Jpan, Latn, Arab)

uiLanguage.description: Language used for instructions/translations within this pack (e.g. tr means lessons explain Japanese in Turkish)

license.description: SPDX license identifier (e.g. CC-BY-4.0, MIT, CC-BY-SA-4.0)

dependencies.description: Other packs this one builds on (by id and version range)

minSdkVersion.description: Minimum SDK version required to load this pack

aiCapabilities.description: Optional. Declares which AI features this pack expects to support. The SDK uses these flags to decide which AI affordances to surface in the UI; the backend additionally checks the end user's subscription before forwarding to a provider. Pack still works fully offline regardless of these flags.

questionGeneration.description: AI can synthesize new practice questions from this pack's content

explanation.description: AI can give deeper grammar / etymology / context explanations on demand

conversation.description: AI can hold conversation practice using this pack's vocabulary

hint.description: AI can provide context-aware hints during exercises

previousPack.description: Optional. Pack id of the prerequisite pack in a curated level path (e.g. com.paktly.ja.beginner-1)

nextPack.description: Optional. Pack id of the recommended next pack in a curated level path

translationStatus.description: Schema 1.2.0+. Optional. Per-locale provenance signal for the translations the pack ships. Keys are BCP-47 locale codes (must lowercase + optional region/script suffix); values describe how the translation was produced. UI surfaces this so users can distinguish native-quality content from machine-translated material. The registry's `supportedLocales` and `localeCoverage` are derived independently from the actual lesson content; this field is purely a quality declaration by the creator.

^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)?$.description: native = human-authored or curated dictionary. machine = LLM auto-translated, unreviewed. reviewed = machine + human review. partial = some atoms missing (legacy / migrating).
